correctness.rationale: With S=(01)(23) and T=(03)(12) the Gram matrix is (2(r+1)I+rS+T)/6. The commuting involutions diagonalize in the four Hadamard vectors, with eigenvalues of 6G equal to 3(r+1), 3r+1, r+3 and r+1. Inverting and collecting recovers the signed row (A,-B,C,-D) in the frozen proof. Every vertex has that evaluation norm by the half-turn and reflection symmetries; interpolation gives an upper bound by the nodal norms throughout each edge. The real sign of the reproducing kernel is an evaluating extremizer for bounded inputs, also valid on the complex space. Continuity of its projected output makes the vertex value relevant to the essential supremum. Continuous sign approximations give the C-to-C norm, and bounded symmetric kernel duality gives the L1 norm. The absolute integral on a sign-changing affine edge is the sum of two triangle areas. Equivalently, from the row's signed kernel integral 1, add rB²/(A+B)+B²/(B+C)+rD²/(C+D)+D²/(D+A). Substitution and collection gives F(r)=5/3+8(u+2)(11u+26)/[3(2u+5)(3u+10)^2], u=r+1/r. Differentiation with respect to u gives -16(33u³+178u²+278u+100)/[3(2u+5)^2(3u+10)^3]. Thus F strictly decreases for u>=2, equals 17/9 at u=2, and is strictly above 5/3 with that limiting value as u tends to infinity. This verifies inversion, both monotone branches and all boundary claims without relying on finite samples. The frozen exact Gram checker and six finite-difference tests were read, not executed.

value.rationale: Four knots are the smallest distinct-vertex circle that realizes nonconstant alternating spacing. The exact shape law gives a usable quantitative benchmark for projecting on that mesh: it distinguishes a strictly worst uniform shape from increasingly degenerate contrasts, with finite-cycle constants different from the repeated-mesh envelope. The value is the full shape-dependent stability profile, not a recomputation at uniform spacing alone.
